full_judgment:
2. Facts in short are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed, above case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of 15 decimals land appertaining to RS, khatian Nos. 376 and 377 as mentioned in the schedule of the petition. 

 3. It was alleged that the petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance in RS khatian No. 377 and co-sharer by purchase to RS khatian No. 376 but the opposite party No. 1 is a stranger to above khatians. Opposite part No. 2 transferred disputed land to opposite party No. 1 by a registered kobla deed on 1-4-1987 without any notice upon the petitioner. The petitioner came to know about above transfer on 20-4-2005 filed this case on 30-4-2005. 

 12. On consideration of above materials on record the learned Additional District Judge has rightly allowed the appeal and pre-emption which calls for no interference. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Judge of court of appeal below erroneously omitted to mention the disputed land of R.S. khatian No. 377 in the operative part partition of the judgment. For rectifying above error opposite party has filed a petition under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the court of appeal which could not be disposed of due to call for of the record by this Court. 

 14. As OPW 1 opposite party No. 1 has admitted in his cross-examination that the petitioner is a cosharer by inheritance to R.S. khatian No. 377 and a co-sharer by purchase to RS khatian No. 376 and he is a stranger to above khatians. It is also admitted that this case was' filed on 30-4-2005 before the impugned kobla deed dated 10-4-2005 was registered under section 60 of the Registration Act, 1925. But the petitioner has removed above deficiency in the court of appeal by reexamining PW 1 and producing a certified copy of the impugned kobla deed. As such this case is neither a premature one nor the same is barred by limitation.
